steps.title: Look at two ways of saying the same thing.
steps.sub: There’s a mistake in the bill. · There seems to be a mistake in the bill.
steps.prompt: Why does the customer add “seems to be”?
options: It softens the complaint and does not accuse anyone.
It means the customer is not sure the bill exists.
It is more formal but means something different.
steps.answer: It softens the complaint and does not accuse anyone.
steps.why: There seems to be lets you raise a problem without saying “you made a mistake”.

steps.title: Dealing with a problem in a restaurant
steps.html:
What you are doingWhat you say
raising the problemExcuse me. There seems to be a mistake in the bill.
saying you can’t eat itI’m afraid I can’t eat this — it doesn’t smell fresh.
asking for somethingCould I have another glass, please? / Could you possibly bring me a cloth?
asking for timeWould you mind waiting while I get some money?
apologising (you)I’m very sorry — I’ve just spilt my juice.
apologising (the waiter)I’m terribly sorry. / I do apologize. / I’ll get you another one.
accepting an apologyDon’t worry about it. / It’s not your fault.

Start with Excuse me and, in English, keep your voice level. Politeness does the work, not volume.

Could you possibly …? and Would you mind …ing? are the two most polite requests. Notice that would you mind takes the -ing form.

I’m afraid softens bad news, exactly as it did at the hotel in Lesson 21.

I do apologize is stronger than I apologize — the do adds weight. Staff use it; customers rarely need it.

You already met I’m writing to complain about … in Lesson 15. This lesson is the spoken version.

steps.title: Restaurant review · model
steps.html:
A review of the restaurant, written the next day. You will write your own at the end.

Kausar — good food, one long wait

Kausar · Karaganda · 3 / 5   Visited on Saturday evening, two people

The place. Kausar is a small family restaurant behind the market. The atmosphere is warm and slightly noisy, which we liked. The tables are close together, so it is not the place for a quiet conversation.

The food. The lamb tagine was excellent — the meat is cooked for hours and it comes apart with a fork. The portions are large. My friend’s fish, though, was overcooked and quite dry, and it arrived twenty minutes after my dish.

The service. The waiter apologized immediately, took the fish away and did not charge us for it. That is how a problem should be handled, and it changed our evening.

Value. Two courses and water came to 6,400 tenge for two people. For that quality, it is good value.

The only downside was the wait for the second dish. I’d recommend Kausar for a weekday evening, and I’d recommend booking if you go at the weekend.

steps.title: Write a review of a restaurant you know.
steps.sub: About 150–200 words. Follow the five parts of the model, and include one negative point.
steps.html:
1. Plan (from the model): the place and the atmosphere → the food, good and bad → the service → the value → the one downside and your recommendation.
  • <b>The place.</b> … The atmosphere is …
  • <b>The food.</b> … was excellent, but …
  • <b>The service.</b> The waiter …
  • <b>Value.</b> … came to …
  • The only downside was … I’d recommend …
The atmosphere isThe portions areis cookedwas overcookedthe service wasgood valueThe only downside wasI’d recommendbookingapologizedbill
steps.modelHtml:
• I wrote about the place, the food, the service and the value.
  • I gave one clear negative point, not only praise.
  • I used at least two passives (is cooked, was overcooked).
  • I ended with a recommendation.
  • I did not use informal chat language.
